Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Geoffroi de Villehardouin (author, Wikidata Q5361), died 1213; Frank T. Marzials (translator, Wikidata Q18911590), died 1912. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Villehardouin, Geoffroi de, 1150-1213?") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: Geoffroi de Villehardouin [1210, 1213]).

Printed edition: Chronicle of the Fourth Crusade and the Conquest of Constantinople, 1908, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/isbn_9781530697205. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 97%, 94%, 92% of their four-word runs in the scan's text.
